firestore.reasoning: The Firestore data structure is designed to store user profiles and user-generated music scores (posts). It prioritizes authorization independence and simplifies security rules by leveraging path-based ownership for user data. Each user has a dedicated collection for their posts, located at `/users/{userId}/posts/{postId}`. This structure inherently enforces ownership, as only the user with the matching `userId` can access the documents within their collection. This eliminates the need for complex `get()` calls in security rules, ensuring atomicity for operations and straightforward debugging. QAPs (Rules are not Filters) is ensured as access to posts are filtered based on the userId, which is available in `request.auth.uid`.
